status_note: Reproduces on Spark 4.3.0, the latest release, in both ANSI modes; main not read. No upstream issue found in ASF JIRA; related, other functions: SPARK-60073 (`try_make_timestamp`), SPARK-47571 (`date_format`).
title: `to_timestamp` past the microsecond range raises a bare `ArithmeticException`
summary: `to_timestamp` of a year past the microsecond range raises a bare `java.lang.ArithmeticException: long overflow` with no error class or SQLSTATE, in both ANSI modes. The parser's `extractMicros` multiplies the epoch seconds with `Math.multiplyExact`; under ANSI `parseToTimestampExact` wraps only `DateTimeException` and `ParseException` in an error class, and without ANSI `isParseError` turns only those into NULL, so the overflow escapes both.
repro:
SELECT to_timestamp('294248', 'y');
-- java.lang.ArithmeticException: long overflow (no error class), ANSI on or off
handling: The profile must treat the timestamp range as a precondition on parsed values or refuse the construct. The reference raises far earlier (`date_range`, 9999-12-31), so a guarded plan never reaches it. The fix upstream is to catch the `ArithmeticException` in `extractMicros` and raise `DATETIME_OVERFLOW`, or NULL under `try_to_timestamp` and without ANSI.
found_by: Spark's SQL query tests at v4.3.0 (sverify_dev.spark_tests, Spark evidence session): datetime-parsing-invalid.sql
